comment: SOOO nice and funny! Ignore the weird reviews!

Humorous and passionate professor. Very caring for students. He always wants you to do better, but still respects your choices if you feel you are doing okay. One of the most friendly professor I meet in UR and really makes the class warm and welcome, especially for first-year students. If you need to general edu requirement, choose THTR 207 !!!

Film 1960s is a super easy FYS. He is an easy grader on essays, and often lets class out 20-40 minutes early. You do have to participate though to do well, however you don't have to read or even buy the books. You pretty much watch movies, take easy quizes on the movies, do 1 project, and write 3 papers. Also is a funny and kinda guy in general.

He is very knowledgable and chill. He ends class early all the time. You will learn quite a lot, he doesn't assign homeworks but the written assignments are really hard because you don't know what he expects from you, he does not put documents specifying what to write about for the assignments. Apart from the unclearness he is a very likeable guyS

Walter is a crazy professor, always cracking jokes no one understood followed by a sudden and startling laugh. he was not at all clear with what he wanted on his essays and most class discussions were simply people throwing out opinions so when it came time to write an essay you had no clue how to unless you read the book.

Walter is definitely different than most professors you will have in college. If you are interested in the topic like I was you will enjoy his class, but if not you will probably find him really boring. Fair grader but didn't hand anything back until the last week of classes. You don't really need to do the readings, but class participation is key.

The problem is that I have no idea what my grade is right now and I find the class boring. We have 1 month until this class is over and he hasn't even handed us our first assignment back yet. Also I have no interest in theater, so at first I was really intimidated by this class, but there is basically no homework

Walter is an awesome guy! His credentials are ASTOUNDING, and he is extremely knowledgeable. He is hilarious, and as long as you pay attention in his class you cant go wrong. Loved his FYS Films of the 1930's.

Honestly, I can understand why non-theatre students just wouldn't get Walter.  However, if you are open-minded and appreciate him in terms of his industry, he's a great resource.  When I graduate, I will be proud to say that I studied under him.  (Also, he once accidentally split my lip at a rehearsal...passionate is right.)

Walter is AMAZING. He inspired me to choose theatre as my major. Taking one of his classes, even if you're not a major of minor is definitely worth your time. He doesn't grade too harshly, as long as you spend time on the work. Hands down the best professor I've had at UR. If you can handle Walter's eccentricities, you'll love him.

This class is WORK. I am not a theater person, and I took the class to fulfill my requirement. It was enjoyable- I looked foward to going to class and hearing Schoen's anecdotes and extremely knowledgable advice- but he assigned a lot of homework. He is nit-picky about performances, but hes knows a lot about his field. Quizzes are hard, do your hw.

Mr. Schoen, while being a bit unclear about assignment requirements at times, is a really great guy once you get to know him. Very animated and eccentric for sure. His workload is fairly light (for a UR class) and he makes class fun and interesting. If looking to fill a requirement in performing arts, take his class!

I never had Walter for CORE or any intro classes, but he's the best script analysis and directing teacher I could have hoped for.  Walter holds you to his own high standards which is why his classes are so difficult, but he also understands the demands of the theatre major, so he extended a few deadlines for us which was very nice of him, and not at all necessary.  He's a very passionate and sensitive man, and he cares a lot about acting and directing.  It'll be challenging, but you'll thank yourself later.

I thought he did an okay job teaching acting to many people who had no real interest in it (read: several football players in class). Strange guy, tough to read. I thought he was fair and has a good background for the class.

Walter is the best professor I had at UR.  His credentials go beyond his theatrical or teaching resume, and his precious lessons come from his unique and fully engaged perception of the human condition.  He was more than a professor, he was a mentor who encouraged me to raise the bar I set for myself as he constantly raises the bar set for him.

He is a great teacher if you can break out of the normal class mode and just have a discussion.  He may not be great at handing back papers, but there aren't many other people I would rather have directing me or leading a discussion.  And I've had many classes with him.
crazy mofo but insightful
ok, the man is a nutcase. stay away, FAR away

The University of Richmond should be extremely ashamed to have a professor like him teach here. He does not have the capabilities or the credentials to teach. He lacks commitment and is not prompt, always late for class and never hands back any work. He just is plain simply horrible.

I think he should have never received a teaching degree. He never graded anything. He was completely inappropriate in the classroom. Richmond should be embarassed to have hired him, and he certainly should not be teaching the freshman core class.

Walter does sway over the spectrum of emotions, but he seems to have the students' education at heart, without succumbing to the whims of administration.  If that makes sense.  And he is a great speaker.
He is amusing in class, but dont get on his bad side. Also he never hands any graded papers back so your grade is a complete surprise at the end of the semester.

Walter is a character. He knows a lot about a lot of things, and brings a lot to the class. He's pretty interesting for Core. However, he does kind of have a temper. Not too bad though, I'd still recommend him. He must be a riot in theater classes.
